title: Reading Shakespeare in context
keyIdea: Shakespeare's English is mostly our English, with a few old words to swap, such as thou for you and wherefore for why. Paraphrase a speech to find what the character means, not just the picture the words paint. Then read it the way a 1606 audience would: they believed God chose the king and that witches were real, so killing King Duncan breaks the whole order of nature.

kid: Shakespeare wrote Macbeth in about 1606. His English is early modern English. Most of the words are ours. A few small ones change the meaning, so learn them first. Thou means you. Art means are. Hath means has. Wherefore means why, not where.

To paraphrase, put a line into your own words. Keep the meaning, not the picture. When Macbeth says, “Stars, hide your fires,” he does not want the stars to die. He wants it dark, so no one sees the murder he is planning.

Now read it like his first audience. Many people then believed God ranked all things in a chain. God was at the top, then angels, then the king, then nobles, then everyone else, then animals. So killing a king was a crime against God. After Duncan dies, the play shows nature going wrong. Day stays dark, an owl kills a falcon, and horses eat each other.

The king who watched this play was James the First. He wrote a book about witches and believed they were real. He was also said to come from the family of Banquo. So the witches were truly scary to that audience, and Banquo is shown as good. Use context like this to explain a line, not as a fact stuck on the end.
adult: This topic asks learners to read a Shakespeare play in depth. They follow plot, character and theme through early modern English. They also link ideas to what people in the time of Elizabeth and James believed about kings, women, fate and order. The lab uses Macbeth, the most widely taught play at this stage.

In the lab, learners match old words to their meanings and fix paraphrases of a key speech. They rebuild the Great Chain of Being and find the signs of nature in disorder after the murder. Then they link details of the play to events of 1606, such as King James's book on witches and the trial of a priest tied to the Gunpowder Plot.

Common mistakes: reading wherefore as where; paraphrasing word by word, so the images are taken literally; judging the play only by modern values; and adding context that explains nothing, such as Shakespeare's birth date. Another slip is to say a character changes without quoting the start and the end.

Ask your teenager to paraphrase one famous speech aloud, line by line. Then ask how the first audience would have felt about it, and why. A strong answer links a belief of the time to particular words in the play.

familyTip: Pick a famous line, such as “Fair is foul, and foul is fair.” Take turns putting it into everyday words, then ask: why would this have scared people who believed witches were real?

practice.prompt: Juliet says, “Wherefore art thou Romeo?” What is she asking?
choices: Why are you Romeo, a Montague?
Where are you, Romeo?
Who are you, Romeo?
practice.hint: Wherefore is an old word. Is it where, why or who?
practice.explain: Wherefore means why. Juliet knows where Romeo is not the point: she wishes he were not from the family her own family hates.

practice.prompt: A king says, “Thou hast but {n} days to live.” What does this mean in modern English?
choices: You have only {n} days to live.
Where are your {n} days to live?
They have {n} days to live.
practice.hint: Swap thou for you and hast for have. What does but mean here?
practice.explain: Thou is you and hast is have. But here means only, so the line is: you have only {n} days to live.

practice.prompt: After Duncan's murder, his horses turn wild and eat each other. Why does Shakespeare include this?
choices: Nature itself is thrown into disorder by killing a king
To add a scene about animals
To show the horses were hungry
practice.hint: Think of the Great Chain of Being. What happens when one link breaks?
practice.explain: A king was believed to be chosen by God. Killing him breaks the chain, so nature turns upside down: animals attack their betters and day becomes night.

practice.prompt: Lady Macbeth says, “Ere {n} o’clock, the deed is done.” What does ere mean?
choices: Before
After
Where
practice.hint: Ere is an old word for time. Try each choice in the sentence.
practice.explain: Ere means before. The line means: before {n} o’clock, the deed is done.

choices: People in 1606 believed God chose kings, so Duncan's murder is a crime against heaven.
Shakespeare was born in 1564.
Macbeth is a play with five acts.
practice.hint: Good context explains something in the play. Which one does?
practice.explain: Only the first links a belief of the time to an event in the play. A birth date or the number of acts explains nothing about what the play means.

pool.prompt: In 1606, who did most people believe had chosen the king?
choices: God
The people, by voting
The richest nobles
pool.hint: This belief is called the divine right of kings.
pool.explain: Under the divine right of kings, God chose the monarch. King James wrote that kings answer to God alone, so a murdered king was an attack on God's order.

pool.prompt: The witches chant, “Fair is foul, and foul is fair.” What does it mean?
choices: Things that look good may be evil, and evil may look good
The weather is bad today
Fair people are always foul
pool.hint: Fair can mean good or lovely. Foul means evil or ugly.
pool.explain: The witches warn that nothing is what it seems. That idea runs through the play: Macbeth looks loyal while planning murder.

pool.prompt: In Act 4, the witches show Macbeth a line of eight kings who come from Banquo. Why might this please the first audience?
choices: King James was said to descend from Banquo
Banquo was Shakespeare's father
Audiences liked long parades
pool.hint: Who was the king in 1606, and whose family was he said to come from?
pool.explain: King James was said to come from Banquo's family, so the scene flatters him. It also explains why Banquo is shown as loyal and good.

pool.prompt: Lady Macbeth asks spirits to “unsex me here.” Which belief of the time is she going against?
choices: Women should be gentle and obey their husbands
Women should rule the country
Women should fight in wars
pool.hint: She asks to lose something her time expected of women. What was it?
pool.explain: Women were expected to be gentle and obedient. She asks to lose that softness so she can plan a murder, which would have shocked the audience.

pool.prompt: A student quotes {n} lines of a speech in a row and writes nothing about them. What is missing?
choices: A paraphrase and a comment on what the words show
More lines of quotation
The date the play was written
pool.hint: Quotes are evidence. What must you do with evidence?
pool.explain: Long quotes on their own prove nothing. Quote a few words, say what they mean in your own words, then explain what they show about the character or theme.

pool.prompt: The Porter jokes about an “equivocator” at the gate of hell. Why would that land in 1606?
choices: A priest linked to the Gunpowder Plot had just defended equivocation at his trial
Equivocators were a type of soldier
It was a popular song
pool.hint: To equivocate is to twist words to avoid the truth. Who was in the news for it?
pool.explain: In 1606 a priest, Henry Garnet, was tried for his part in the Gunpowder Plot and defended equivocation. The joke ties Macbeth's lies to a real treason against the king.

pool.prompt: Early on, Macbeth is called “brave Macbeth.” At the end, he is “this dead butcher.” What does this show?
choices: He changes from a hero to a tyrant
He was always a butcher
Nothing about him changes
pool.hint: Compare the two names. What happened in between?
pool.explain: The names bookend his change: from a loyal, brave soldier to a murderous tyrant. Quoting the start and the end is how to prove a character changes.

pool.prompt: Why did the witches frighten audiences in 1606 more than most people today?
choices: Many, King James included, believed witches were real and served the devil
Witches were a new idea in 1606
The actors wore scary masks
pool.hint: What did King James write a book about in 1597?
pool.explain: King James wrote Daemonologie, a book about witches, and witch trials were real. To the first audience, the witches were a real danger, not fantasy.

pool.prompt: A messenger says, “I shall be with thee ere {n} days are past.” What does he promise?
choices: I will be with you before {n} days have passed.
I will be with you after {n} days.
Where will you be in {n} days?
pool.hint: Swap thee for you and ere for before.
pool.explain: Thee is you and ere is before, so he will arrive within {n} days, not after them. Reading ere as after reverses the promise.

visual.caption: Does this context explain the play? Drag each fact, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: James was said to descend from Banquo

lab.caption: Flagship lab: decode old words, paraphrase Macbeth's speech, rebuild the Great Chain of Being, spot nature in disorder and link the play to 1606.
